claims.sentence: On World Hepatitis Day, 28 July 2026, WHO/Europe said the European Region has made progress against hepatitis but millions still miss diagnosis and treatment.
claims.evidence: WHO/Europe release: progress in Europe but millions miss diagnosis and treatment

claims.sentence: WHO/Europe published the statement on World Hepatitis Day, 28 July 2026, and it concerns the WHO European Region, not the world as a whole.
claims.evidence: Release dated 28-07-2026 on the WHO European Region

claims.sentence: The Region has already met its hepatitis B elimination target for children under 5, with prevalence at about 0.06%.
claims.evidence: Region surpassed hep B elimination target in under-5s, prevalence est. 0.06%

claims.sentence: The Region remains off track for all of its 2030 hepatitis elimination targets.
claims.evidence: WHO/Europe says region remains off-track to achieve all hepatitis elimination targets by 2030

claims.sentence: WHO/Europe says only 23% of people with hepatitis B have been diagnosed and 4.2% are receiving treatment.
claims.evidence: Only 23% of people with hep B diagnosed, 4.2% receiving treatment

claims.sentence: On World Hepatitis Day, 28 July 2026, the World Health Organization's European regional office (WHO/Europe) reported on progress against hepatitis in the WHO European Region.
claims.evidence: Release dated 28-07-2026 on WHO European Region

claims.sentence: It says the Region has already met its hepatitis B elimination target for children under 5 years, with prevalence at about 0.06%.
claims.evidence: Region surpassed hep B target among children under 5, prevalence ~0.06%

claims.sentence: New hepatitis B infections are down 54% since 2015 and new hepatitis C infections are down 28%.
claims.evidence: Hep B infections down 54% since 2015, hep C down 28%

claims.sentence: The Region is still off track for all of its 2030 elimination targets.
claims.evidence: Region remains off-track to achieve all hepatitis elimination targets by 2030

claims.sentence: WHO/Europe estimates that 9.7 million people live with hepatitis B and 5.6 million with hepatitis C in the Region, and that only 23% of people with hepatitis B have been diagnosed and 4.2% are receiving treatment.
claims.evidence: 9.7 million hep B, 5.6 million hep C; 23% diagnosed, 4.2% treated

claims.sentence: WHO/Europe's regional adviser says the main gap is now finding people and getting them into care, rather than prevention.
claims.evidence: Bivol: biggest gap today is no longer prevention but finding people and ensuring care

claims.sentence: The 2026 World Hepatitis Day theme is "Hepatitis: Let's break it down", and the WHO is urging countries to remove barriers to testing and treatment.
claims.evidence: Theme 'Hepatitis: Let's break it down' on WHO campaign page; Europe release asks countries to remove barriers to testing and treatment

notes: Search summaries were inconsistent once on whether 'off track' wording appears; a later targeted search returned 'remains off-track to achieve all hepatitis elimination targets by 2030' from the WHO/Europe release, so kept.
